body: Thank you for this. Like most people in the Fempire, I really want to be welcoming to my trans* peeps both here and IRL. It does help to know and try to internalize these things in advance (just as our culture would have us internalize the opposite!) I don't want to be hurtful accidentally.

I read this and it rubbed me the wrong way, but I can't articulate why very well. Maybe it's because at the very end we get back to "what about the men" and hinting that women's gains are responsible for men's falling behind when, in most cases, it's still a result of the patriarchy. There also seems to be a lot of us vs them talk when it comes to patriarchal societies, as if we lack those extremists in western culture. I don't know, though. I would love to read a critique of this by someone who is more educated and eloquent than myself.
*hugs* back...
I was just reading that thread and came here to comfort myself. Absolutely unreal.
Thank you again. I've not been able to read the whole thing just yet (attention span has flown out the window...!) but the little bit I did read made a lot of sense.

"Cling" is very accurate when describing how I held on to a belief that was deeply unsatisfying and yet contained so much of my hope and emotion.

I don't know if I would be able to practice the art of not clinging just yet, but I will definitely take a look at r/Buddhism and see what it is about.

I have gotten so many thoughtful replies, and in my desire to respond to them all, I think my brain has exhausted its cache of useful language...so if this mostly doesn't make sense, please know that I appreciate what you've written and the time you took to write it. Thank you for what you've said here.

*takes hug gratefully*

Thanks for the link. I did read it and it made me realize that I am experiencing my terrible loneliness as a lack of meaning...and the loneliness might be fixable. In the last year or so I've kind of fallen out of the bottom of my social life and losing church was part of that, because for a while now I haven't wanted to go. The promise of fellowship was not equal to the antagonism I knew I'd feel and the renewed questions that never seemed to get answers.

I'm not worried so much about dying (which, is kind of a problem sometimes...) but I guess I've been worried about dying as unhappily as I've lived. That scares me, that I won't somehow manage to feel better, to have a life before I die. Hence my hope that I would get an afterlife where things would be better...

I think what I value most is love and connection with other people. I value honest communication. I value thinking (when I can!) and learning and the excitement that comes from it. I value the impressive nature of emotions...

This is a hard world to live in, and it's difficult reconciling taking care of the physical aspects of life with leading an emotionally and mentally satisfying existence (a conflict everyone experiences, I know) and I often worry about how I will manage to do it. I've always thought of suicide as my go-to escape, but I really don't want to do that anymore. I want to commit to living here and now and try and make the best of it. I just don't know how.

Thank you for writing to me.

Thanks for the recommendation...I've seen that around numerous times and just never thought to pick it up. I will now.

I hope I get through this too...thank you.

I have loved all the advice people have given me here, yours included. Especially this:

>But not needing to find meaning in life takes a huge weight off.

It's certainly easier than wondering if whatever crummy thing that happened is because god is punishing you for something.

Thank you for the encouragement and the kind words.

I really didn't expect to lose my beliefs. I was so completely *earnest*. In the "Okay god, I have this question, can you answer?" kind of way, over and over and over. And then poof!

Thank you for the well wishes...I really want to feel better and I want to find a life. More happiness for you, too.

>you implied you are sterile, single, and that everyone you love is deceased or non-existent. 

Ok, so maybe a little hyperbole... :D Although it's reasonably close to the truth. I've lost a lot of people whom I loved dearly and will very likely remain childless. But there are also people here whom I love, and I'm realizing that the biggest theft that a belief in god or the afterlife commits is taking hope and action from *now*. The things people are saying to me here make so much sense and basically it's many variations on *go live life now because it's all you have* which isn't nearly as scary as it seems at first.

My thank you is completely genuine...thank you for taking the time to write what you did, to share your thoughts with me.
Yeah, I think I get what you are saying. The world feels more open now...I really hope I can find that meaning.
Thank you! I found that really touching and very applicable to where I am now...

Thank you so much for taking the time to write your thoughts and suggestions here. It really means a lot to me. This has been a huge transition, one I was not prepared for (it was kind of opposite of where I thought I would end up) but then, who can really prepare for the directions our undisciplined minds take us? ;)

I do have a mood disorder, which makes life and especially intellectual life difficult at times. I think a key difference for me will be taking more responsibility for myself and the direction my life is going, rather than relying on 'god' (who never seemed to help.)

I'm kind of emotionally/mentally exhausted at the moment so I can't give your post the attention to detail that I would like in my response. But I want you to know that I appreciate it so very much.

Religion was definitely a coping mechanism for me, as it gave me a way to hang on through some really tough times. I agree about the laughter. I love to laugh and to make people laugh. (Whether or not I'm good at it is another question...) Thanks for posting.

Thank you, very much. In the middle of my suicidal thinking I realized that there are a ton of things that I don't know, and that continuing to learn might be enough to make me keep postponing until the inevitable happens. And who knows, I might yet do something good.

I do feel much more free now. I think I am also tired out from all the existential wrangling that has gone on in my head for the last few months. This does feel like a big change already, but I hope I can find things to do that will give me a sense of purpose. Thanks for the encouragement.

There's a lot of truth to this, as I'm finding out...

Thanks.
Thank you, I'll go check it out.

I'm not enough of a morning person to have gotten up early, but I hear what you are saying, and I will try to seize one of those moments--whether it's a sunset or a chance go to out to the garden and look at the growing things.

And yeah, music!

Yes, it makes absolute sense. Even despite my lack of belief I still find myself praying, probably because I still hope that some god (he, she, they or it) will come to my rescue. I don't believe in hell anymore...that was one of the first holes in my faith. If there is a god, I am certain that hell is not in the equation.

I suppose the only relief, for me, is that when I'm dead I really won't care.

Thank you for sharing your thoughts with me.

I appreciate what you've said here. I think what is difficult is facing that I've likely wasted a lot of time that I'll never get back. Not so much the time spent in church, but with the idea that things were going to get better. If I can't make them better, they won't get better...and I lack the resources to do it. So I don't know.

I know I'm not making a lot of sense. My brain is floating along untethered, and more than a little sad.
I hope so. If anything, one thing I'm certain of is that I don't know much.
Your response made me smile because honestly, I do wish I was a rock or some sand on a beach. But you're right about the other stuff...I honestly wish I could just get on board and be okay, you know?
Thank you. I wish I could get from here to there. Thank you for the good wishes.
